title: Producers: acknowledgements, idempotence, and duplicate business events
outcome: Distinguish client retry deduplication from repeated application publication.
useCase: Reliable publication of saved Rails events.
benefits: Clear publication evidence and stable retry identity.
drawbacks: The DB/Kafka publication gap still permits repeats.
version: Kafka 4.1 KRaft · lab Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 · legacy Rails adaptation notes
cue: Buffer accepted ≠ broker acknowledged ≠ business completed.

trace.title: Stable event ID
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A producer serializes a record and asks a partition leader to append it. Its delivery handle/future reports the result under the client configuration.

Enqueueing into a client buffer is not the same as an acknowledged broker append.

acks, replica/min-ISR settings, retry limits, and delivery timeouts interact. Idempotent producer support prevents certain retry duplicates under the protocol/session contract.

It does not recognize that two separate application calls with different identities mean the same business completion.

Always carry a stable business event ID. In the outbox, retrying the same saved event preserves that ID.

A consumer can then deduplicate the business effect even when the application re-publishes after a crash.

Choose and verify settings for the actual client library; Ruby librdkafka options are not every Java default pasted unchanged.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Saved event E → client buffer → batch send → broker acknowledgement → mark outbox published. Crash after acknowledgement but before the DB mark means E may be published again.

The producer’s protocol identity does not make the DB mark and Kafka append one transaction. The consumer inbox is still needed for this gap.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
Fire-and-forget publication can lose errors. Producer idempotence is often overclaimed as exactly-once business processing.

App-level resends remain a distinct duplicate source.
